items.title: KLIA security: someone, somewhere is failing to do their job
items.summary: Airport security meant little more than a quick pat-down by personnel armed with hand-held metal detector wands. Nobody asked you to remove your shoes, belt, watch, bangle, jacket, coat, hat, bandana or whatever else airport security happened to take an interest in that particular day. These incidents triggered a sweeping overhaul of airport security worldwide — shoes had to come off, liquids, gels and aerosols were restricted from carry-on luggage, full-body scanners using advanced imaging technology were installed, and bomb-sniffing dogs were brought in to bolster airport security.

items.title: Sime Darby's growth engine shifts into higher gear
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A stronger core, leaner balance sheet and regional diversification are giving Sime Darby Bhd room to navigate intensifying competition and global uncertainty. It is also the outcome of a deliberate strategy centred on focusing the group on automotive and industrial equipment across Asia Pacific. The acquisition of UMW Holdings Bhd has also strengthened Sime Darby's automotive earnings base.

items.title: No Middle East data centre windfall, but Malaysia eyes next wave
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is unlikely to inherit a windfall of data centre investments from the Middle East despite rising geopolitical tensions, but the turmoil could strengthen its hand in the race for the next wave of global digital infrastructure spending. Industry experts said billions of dollars in projects already committed in the Middle East are unlikely to be uprooted, particularly those backed by sovereign wealth funds and tied to national artificial intelligence (AI) and economic ambitions. "Data centres are long-term investments.

items.title: Trump insists Netanyahu relationship 'very good' despite Gaza rift
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump insisted Monday that his relationship with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is "very good" despite the Israeli leader's rejection of a US-led Gaza plan. After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism, Netanyahu explicitly stated on Sunday that he opposed the Gaza plan, which called for Israel to begin pulling back forces in tandem with disarmament by Hamas. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is running even or trailing in some polls ahead of October 27 elections, the country's first since the devastating 2023 attack by Hamas that sparked the Gaza war.

items.title: Special Dewan sitting today to deliberate Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat is set to convene a special meeting today to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will begin the proceedings with an explanation session on the RCI report. Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the special parliamentary session s on Tuesday would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.

items.title: Drought declared in 'almost three-quarters' of England: UK govt
items.summary: LONDON: Some 71.3 per cent of England is in drought, the UK government said Monday, after the nation experienced its driest July on record, with a fifth heatwave and scant rain forecast for the week ahead. "Almost three-quarters of England is now in drought as conditions worsen following a dry start to August," the environment department said, as parts of the central Midlands and northeast England joined other areas of the country experiencing prolonged dry weather. The Department of Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) said most of England is experiencing a "flash drought", which develops quickly and is the result of very low rainfall and high temperatures.

items.title: Masked man sets woman on fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 62-year-old woman suffered first-degree burns after an unidentified man doused her with petrol and set her alight as she was opening a four-digit gaming outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong on Sunday. Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng's personal secretary, Dic Lai, who met Gan's children at his service centre yesterday, said the family remained in shock over the incident. Lai said Gan contacted one of her five children while waiting for an ambulance to arrive.

items.title: Simplified: The Tabung Haji RCI report and what it said
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Today, in a special sitting of Parliament, MPs are expected to debate a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the country’s Muslim pilgrims’ fund Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Currently, TH manages the savings of over 9.8 million depositors. What is the RCI about?

items.title: Colombia in state of emergency as quake kills 111
items.summary: PEREIRA, Colombia: Colombia declared a state of emergency on Monday after a powerful earthquake killed at least 111 people, damaged more than 1,500 buildings and left an unknown number of people buried under rubble. The 7.4 magnitude quake shook several cities across Colombia's coffee-producing region and the Pacific coast, sending terrified residents racing into the street. "People were praying in the street.

items.title: Trump says will demand conflict compensation from Iran
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Monday he would seek conflict compensation from Iran as part of any peace negotiations, citing attacks and killings stretching back decades allegedly backed or perpetrated by Teheran. Trump's announcement was a direct response to Iran's insistence that US payment of war reparations are a pre-condition to any resolution of the ongoing hostilities. "I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran," he said, noting that his demand included not only damages arising from the current war, but also Iranian attacks on US targets going back more than two decades as well as payments to the families of Iranian protestors killed by authorities over the past 50 years.

items.title: 'Myanmar refugees Asean's responsibility'
items.summary: THE issue of Myanmar refugees is Asean's collective responsibility, with lasting stability in the country crucial to stemming the flow of people fleeing abroad, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. "This is an issue Malaysia must manage under Asean. "That is why Asean centrality on the Myanmar issue is important.

items.title: Government revives 1,647 abandoned housing projects
items.summary: THE government has rehabilitated 1,647 abandoned private housing projects, with a gross development value of around RM153 billion, since 2022, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said yesterday this was part of the government's mission to eliminate abandoned housing projects by 2030, a key target under the newly launched National Housing Policy 2026-2035. These include the housing integrated management system, electronic sales and purchase agreements (e-SPAs) and scheduled audits of housing development accounts.

items.title: From 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysia'
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping jobs and industries, making early talent development critical to Malaysia's economy, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. Citing the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, Akmal said 170 million new jobs could be created globally by 2030, while 92 million jobs may be displaced. He said Malaysia must strengthen its talent pipeline to support the shift towards high-growth, high-value industries, especially semiconductors.

items.title: Burnham vows to end 'subscription traps'
items.summary: PRIME Minister Andy Burnham has vowed to crack down on hard-to-cancel subscriptions and fake discounts as part of measures to tackle the cost-of-living crisis, said Downing Street on Sunday. Burnham said "people are sick and tired of rip-off discounts and subscription traps", where subscriptions are hard to cancel or automatically renew at a higher cost. British consumers are "spending an estimated £1.6 billion a year on (subscriptions) they don't actually want", said Downing Street.

items.title: Days of heavy rain leave at least 16 dead in Philippines
items.summary: MANILA: Floods, landslides and accidents driven by a nine-day downpour equivalent to more than a month's worth of rain in some areas have killed at least 16 people in the northern Philippines, rescuers said Monday. Three people remain unaccounted for. "The rainfall recorded for August 1-9 was highest in Baguio, with an accumulated 1,413.2 millimetres (56 inches)," he said, adding the city's typical downpour for the month was 963.2 millimetres.

items.title: US left-wing star reveals decision to freeze her eggs
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, one of the most prominent figures on the US left and a potential presidential contender, has revealed she is freezing her eggs, saying she wants to speak openly about choices confronting women balancing careers and family. Her disclosure came as speculation mounts over her political future. She said going public about freezing her eggs carried a "political risk," arguing women running for office face questions about marriage and children rarely asked of men.

items.title: Former Broadcasting DG Abdul Rahman Hamid dies at 73
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Broadcasting director-general Datuk Abdul Rahman Hamid has died due to a lung infection at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) yesterday. His son, Mohamed Reza, when contacted yesterday, confirmed that Abdul Rahman died at 5.51pm after receiving treatment at the hospital for about a month. Abdul Rahman served as broadcasting director-general for six years, from 2003 to 2009.

items.title: 107,000ha of forest, land affected by fires in Indonesia as haze fear grows
items.summary: JAKARTA: More than 107,000ha of forest and land have been affected by fires across Indonesia as of Monday, with the government stepping up efforts to prevent transboundary haze from affecting neighbouring countries. Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Djamari Chaniago said Indonesia had received no reports as of Monday that smoke from the fires was affecting other countries. He said six provinces, namely Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan, were being closely monitored as the most critical areas.

items.title: Major quake rocks Colombia and neighbours, at least 18 dead
items.summary: BOGOTA: A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and neighbouring Latin American countries on Monday, with at least 18 people confirmed dead in first reports as shocked residents surveyed destroyed buildings. News footage showed collapsed buildings across western Colombia, though officials said they did not fear a tsunami. It was strong, really strong.

items.title: Humble burrito causes indigestion for Trump's party
items.summary: DEBATE over the price of a burrito is causing indigestion for President Donald Trump's Republican Party, which fears being punished for the high cost of living in November's midterm elections. Not any more, argues Andrew Kolvet, a spokesperson for the conservative youth organisation Turning Point USA (TPUSA). "One of our TPUSA college students gave me his take on affordability: 'A burrito shouldn't cost US$20.'

items.title: Siti Kasim, another activist lose appeal over 2022 rally prohibition order
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today dismissed the appeals by activist Siti Zabedah Kasim, popularly known as Siti Kasim, and another individual challenging a prohibition order obtained by police to bar them from participating in a rally in 2022. In delivering the unanimous decision of the three-member bench, Judge Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli said the prohibition order was validly issued by a magistrate's court. Azhahari also said the prohibition order did not violate Siti Kasim and S.Raveentheran's right to peaceful assembly.

items.title: China is balancing Asia's crude demand by itself
items.summary: If June and July imports are combined, it gives an average of 7.78 million bpd for the past two months. This is 4.21 million bpd below the average of 11.99 million bpd in the three months to the end of February. Asia's total oil imports in July were 22.82 million bpd, according to data compiled by commodity analysts Kpler.

items.title: NST Leader: Growing threat of fake social media accounts
items.summary: THE detection of more than 1,800 fake social media accounts, with many being used to stir up issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R) should concern every Malaysian. Most of these accounts were on Facebook and TikTok, two very popular platforms in Malaysia. The danger is not simply that they are fake accounts.

items.title: Indonesian boy feared drowned after falling into Subang Jaya river
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 8.06pm. He said a team from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, arriving 10 minutes later. He said the search and rescue operation was being hampered by the strong river current.

items.title: Three Malaysians arrested in Taiwan for acting as scam money mules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysians were arrested in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, last month for allegedly acting as money mules for a scam syndicate, reports said. The 39-year-old was arrested in front of a post office ATM, with police seizing NT$155,000 (RM19,660) in cash, two bank cards and a mobile phone. Police seized NT$2,800 (RM355) in cash and two mobile phones from him.

items.title: 100ha forest fire in Sri Aman raises concerns over worsening haze
items.summary: KUCHING: A fire has engulfed about 100ha of forest in Sri Aman, raising concerns that it could worsen the haze situation in Sarawak caused by transboundary smoke. A Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department operations control centre spokesman said the department received an emergency call at 1.19pm, prompting a team from the Sri Aman Fire and Rescue Station to be dispatched to the scene. "Water was also supplied by tankers from the Rural Water Supply Department and the Betong Fire and Rescue Station to replenish the fire engines' water tanks.

items.title: Panic triggers 7-hour sea search for Bangladeshi labourer
items.summary: KUANTAN: A Bangladeshi labourer sparked a seven-hour search-and-rescue operation after jumping into the sea during an Immigration Department inspection at a construction site in Tanjung Lumpur today. Taman Tas Fire and Rescue Department chief Mohd Hilmi Kashfi Mat Zali said the department received information from the Immigration Department at 9.35am about a foreigner who had allegedly drowned after jumping into the sea. The department's Underwater Rescue Team divers were also deployed to assist.

items.title: Zahid visits Ismail Sabri at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today visited former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here. In a post on X, Zahid also prayed for the Bera member of Parliament's recovery and continued good health. Zahid also prayed that Ismail Sabri would be able to resume his service and daily activities as usual.

items.title: UK radio apologises after accidentally announcing King Charles' death
items.summary: LONDON: A community radio station breached the rules after accidentally announcing the death of King Charles III in a May broadcast, a UK watchdog said on Monday. Radio Caroline, a former pirate radio that now mostly plays rock music, apologised in May after airing messages falsely announcing the monarch's death. The presenter apologised 30 minutes after the messages were initially triggered, Ofcom said.

items.title: Another Malaysian arrested for drug smuggling abroad after pilot case in Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian was detained for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than four kilogrammes of hydroponic cannabis through Chennai International Airport in India. Chennai Customs, in a statement published by India's Press Information Bureau yesterday, said the passenger arrived from Bangkok, Thailand on Aug 7. Chennai Customs' Air Intelligence Unit officers detained the passenger for inspection based on profiling.

items.title: Hextar Retail draws 43 sen offer from major shareholder
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Retail Bhd has received a conditional voluntary takeover offer from its largest shareholder, Hextar Portfolio Sdn Bhd, at a cash offer price of 43 sen apiece. Hextar Retail currently has 464.99 million shares in issue, excluding 36.10 million treasury shares, of which Hextar Portfolio holds 142.29 million shares. The 43 sen offer price represents a 7.5 per cent premium to Hextar Retail's last traded price of 40 sen on Aug 7.

items.title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns bright among older Malaysians
items.summary: That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year’s National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating Merdeka (Independence) remain fresh in their minds. The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories. With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.

items.title: PKNS denies RM103.69m losses, RM6.1b debt claims as inaccurate and misleading
items.summary: In a statement today, PKNS said allegations portraying the corporation as being in serious financial difficulty were inaccurate and misleading. “It also does not reflect PKNS’ overall financial position. RAM Ratings continues to maintain its AA1/Stable/P1 rating on PKNS,” the corporation said.

items.title: GPS ready for Sarawak polls regardless of redelineation outcome, says Abang Jo
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 10 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) is ready to face the state election with either the existing number of state seats or an increased number following the proposed redelineation exercise, its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said. If there are 82 seats, then 82 seats. If there are 99 seats, then 99 seats.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report to face Parliament scrutiny tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10— Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will present a ministerial briefing on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020 during a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow. In a 35-second video distributed to the media, Zulkifli said he and Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan would also be involved in winding up the parliamentary debate on the report. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil previously said at least 40 MPs had expressed interest in taking part in the debate.

items.title: Ewon, Donald retain Upko top posts
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Aug 10 — Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Ewon Benedick has retained his position as president of the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko), while Datuk Donald Peter Mojuntin remains deputy president after both posts went uncontested at the party’s 17th Triennial Delegates Conference at the Kadazandusun Cultural Association (KDCA) Hall here today. Also elected unopposed were the five vice-presidents — Jairaiaz Joseph, Datuk Wong Thien Fook, Datuk Pangiran Lalung, Datuk Basari Sarikun and Datuk Dr Laurentius Nayan Ambu. Carlye Lajimin was elected the new Upko Youth chief, with Newbaxter Tibin elected as deputy chief.

items.title: Kroll witness tells High Court she was unsure Jho Low was ‘number one’, confirms Najib received 1MDB funds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — An offshore asset recovery specialist testified in the High Court today that she could not confirm whether fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, was the “number one” figure in the alleged conspiracy involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) funds. Muhammad Shafee asked Barkhouse whether she had come across the name of fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, or Jho Low, during the course of her investigation, to which she answered yes. Barkhouse replied: “Amongst others, yes.”

items.title: Four Indonesian fishermen rescued after vessel sinks in Malaysian waters
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 10 — Four Indonesian fishermen crew members were rescued after their ship KM Samudra Jaya Kelautan sank in Malaysian waters while en route from Tarempa to Batam, Indonesia on August 2. Pahang Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director First Admiral (Maritime) Mazlan Mat Rejab said that all the crew members, aged between 40 and 65, were rescued by a local fishing vessel (VNT) from Pahang that was passing through the incident area the day before yesterday. He said the VNT then took all the victims to the Kuantan Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) Jetty at around 5.30am on August 8.

items.title: HR Ministry: 541 Panasonic workers facing retrenchment to get govt help finding new jobs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is deploying early interventions to ensure that 541 employees of Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd who are facing retrenchment do not experience prolonged unemployment, through income protection assistance, job matching, and skills training. Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said that the “from job loss to new job” approach is being implemented through collaboration between the Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia (JTKSM) and the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) to ensure the welfare and career continuity of the employees are safeguarded. “Kesuma will ensure that employees affected by job loss are given appropriate support and are not left to face this transition period without assistance.

items.title: PKR congress to focus on reforms, economy and party strengthening, says veep Amirudin Shari
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 10 — The 2026 PKR National Congress, to be held this week, will focus on the reform agenda, economic development and strengthening the party, said PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. On the party’s decision to grant Nurul Izzah Anwar temporary leave from her duties as PKR deputy president, Amirudin said it would not affect the proceedings of the congress. On August 6, the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) agreed to grant Nurul Izzah temporary leave from performing her duties as the party’s deputy president, effective after the 2026 PKR National Congress until further notice.

items.title: Police to file for inquest into deadly Durian Tunggal shooting this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Police will be filing an application for an inquest into the shooting incident in Durian Tunggal, Melaka, which claimed the lives of three people on November 24 last year. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the inquest itself will take place in Melaka, although the exact date has yet to be determined. On November 24 last year, three men aged between 24 and 29 were shot dead at an oil palm plantation in Durian Tunggal around 4am.

items.title: Terengganu seeks more rangers to protect new Pulau Bidong state park
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — The Terengganu state government will submit an application to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) for additional rangers following the gazettement of Pulau Bidong as a state park on July 16. Terengganu State Tourism director Datuk Tengku Mohd Ariffin Tengku A. Rahman said the move was important to strengthen monitoring and ensure regular enforcement covering the land areas, islands and waters extending up to one nautical mile. “On July 16, Pulau Bidong was gazetted as a state park.

items.title: Nine-year-old allegedly bullied at Kedah tahfiz school, father claims
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — A couple have claimed that their nine-year-old son was bullied by a 15-year-old student at his school, leaving him with bruises on several parts of his body and face. “I took my son home for a week-long holiday. Syamsul Azrin said he and his wife subsequently lodged a police report on the same day before taking their son to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital for further examination.

items.title: PKR’s Wong Chen resigns Subang parliamentary seat, effective Aug 10, press conference Wednesday
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PKR’s Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as Subang MP, effective 5pm. He said he had met Dewan Rakyat Speaker Johari Abdul on August 5 to hand over his resignation letter, allowing parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy. “We shall also be removing the honorific title of Yang Berhormat from all our billboards, signages and correspondence by next month,” he added.

items.title: Melaka BN free to negotiate, Zahid confirms Ab Rauf empowered to lead coalition seat talks
items.summary: GERIK, Aug 10 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) has been given the green light to hold discussions with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election. As reported by Harian Metro (HM), BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had empowered Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to lead the talks in search of common ground to ensure stable governance in the state. He added that Ab Rauf, who also chairs Melaka BN and Umno state liaison body, would later present the outcome of the discussions to the coalition’s top leadership before any decision is finalised.

items.title: Housing Ministry resolves RM153b worth of sick or abandoned housing projects, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) has resolved 1,647 “sick” and abandoned private housing projects worth RM153 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 homebuyers to date, said its Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said the ministry is targeting zero abandoned housing projects by 2030 as part of the national housing sector reform agenda, supported by several mechanisms. “These mechanisms include the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH), the electronic Sale and Purchase Agreement (e-SPA), periodic audits of the Housing Development Account (HDA), and the Option to Purchase (OTP), which will be introduced later this year,” he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 here today.

items.title: Over 600 emergency pumps ready nationwide as Malaysia braces for El Nino, says Irrigation Dept
items.summary: The portable pumps would be used to channel water supplies to agricultural areas, irrigation schemes and areas experiencing water supply disruptions, as well as to support forest and peatland fire-fighting operations with the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and relevant agencies. In line with the national water sector’s digitalisation agenda, the department uses the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and Pump Tracking System to monitor pump and water gate operations in real time, enabling disruptions or potential damage to be detected early and reducing the risk of water supply disruptions during the El Nino phenomenon. DID also works with state water supply operators to optimise the operation of water intake towers to ensure continuity of water supply to consumers,” it said.

items.title: Any Melaka BN election deal must be made official, says state party chief
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 10 — Any political agreement involving Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election must be formally decided and should not be based on speculation or discussions on social media, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said any negotiations on political cooperation should take into account various factors, including the strengths, weaknesses and advantages of each party before a decision is made. He said parties interested in forming cooperation with BN for the state election were welcome to hold negotiations, but stressed that such talks would not necessarily result in an alliance.

items.title: Three new housing laws planned as govt reviews Strata Management Act, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) plans to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (DPN) 2026-2035. Minister Nga Kor Ming said the move involves three entirely new laws: the Property Development Act, the Building Managers Act, and the Rent Tenancy Act. In parallel, the government will also revise the existing Strata Management Act 2013.

items.title: Doctors confirm elective surgery success, PM Anwar Ibrahim under strict medical watch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has successfully undergone elective laparoscopic surgery to treat an abdominal para umbilical hernia, his medical team confirmed today. The procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of specialist doctors. Anwar is currently undergoing physiotherapy and remains under close observation, Datuk Dr Asri Ranga bin Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the Prime Minister’s medical team, confirmed.

items.title: Pakistan PM wishes ‘brother’ Anwar swift recovery from medical procedure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wishes Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery from a medical procedure that the Malaysian leader is slated to undergo today. “Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures. Earlier, Anwar’s Senior Press Secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said the prime minister was undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of medical specialists.

items.title: Refunds follow furore as Penang cancels 29,240 ANPR summonses, vows manual enforcement only
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) will cancel 29,240 summonses issued under the automated number plate recognition (ANPR) system between 2025 and August this year. Penang local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the city council will also refund a total RM266,160 summons payments that was received in the same period. “The ANPR summons system has been halted entirely so from now onwards, summons will only be issued manually by the enforcement officers,” he said at a press conference on the issue following public furore over limitations of the system.

items.title: Prevention is better than cure: Govt unveils OTP exit clause to stop sick housing projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The government aims to ensure Malaysia has no abandoned housing projects by 2030, with a new Option to Purchase (OTP) mechanism expected to give developers and buyers an earlier avenue to withdraw from projects that may no longer be viable. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism was part of a broader housing reform agenda aimed at preventing projects from becoming sick or abandoned in the first place. Nga said the ministry’s special task force on private-sector sick and abandoned housing projects had resolved 1,647 such projects — as of today — involving RM153 billion and nearly 200,000 homebuyers over the past three years.

items.title: Amirudin Shari: Pakatan open to working with Bersatu, Perikatan if stability maintained
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) prioritises political stability and the people’s interests when considering any form of political cooperation with other parties or coalitions, said PH Presidential Council member Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. The PKR vice-president said PH remained open to establishing cooperation or reaching an understanding with any party or coalition that upheld these two principles. “Cooperation with any party, not just Bersatu or Perikatan Nasional (PN), can be considered, provided the underlying principles remain political stability and the well-being of the people,” he said.

items.title: The death of plastic? E-wallets now displacing credit and debit cards across Malaysia
items.summary: E-wallet usage among non-cash payment users climbed from 52 per cent in 2023 to 81 per cent in 2026 — a jump of nearly 30 percentage points. Over the same period, debit card usage fell from 76 per cent to 56 per cent, and credit card usage nearly halved, from 15 per cent down to 9 per cent. Online banking and digital transfers held comparatively steady, moving from 70 per cent to 70 per cent.

items.title: High Court upholds blogger Jufazli Shi’s acquittal over YouTube post against Ismail Sabri, Umno
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court here today upheld the acquittal of blogger Jufazli Shi Ahmad on two charges of posting offensive communications against former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and UMNO on YouTube and failing to provide police with the password to the account four years ago. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin upheld the Sessions Court’s decision after dismissing the prosecution’s appeal against Jufazli’s acquittal on October 18, 2024, at the end of the prosecution’s case. “After reading the appeal record, the grounds of judgment of the Sessions Court judge and the submissions of both parties, this court dismisses the appellant’s appeal and upholds the decision of the Sessions Court judge to discharge and acquit the appellant,” Aslam said.

items.title: Selangor govt to local councils: Don’t let land go idle, put it to use for urban farming
items.summary: State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said applications could be made to lease the identified land for urban farming activities, including community gardens and programmes carried out by the private sector. He said the move would enable vacant urban land to be managed more systematically while optimising its use for high-value agricultural activities. “The state government has directed local government authorities (PBT) to identify idle land and apply for leases so that the sites can be utilised for community gardens, agricultural programmes or by interested private parties.

items.title: Sarawak schools told to suspend outdoor activities if API exceeds 100
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 10 — All schools in Sarawak have been urged to continuously monitor Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in their respective areas amid the transboundary haze currently affecting the state. It said in areas where API readings exceeded 100, all outdoor activities involving students must be suspended. The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.

items.title: Five men remanded another week over murder of Batu Pahat businessman found in fishing net
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 10 — Five men, who are being investigated in connection with the murder of a businessman here, have been remanded for another week. Their remand is to assist investigators who are probing the murder of a 39-year-old businessman whose bound body was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong in Parit Raja here last week. Their initial remand application ended today.

items.title: Terengganu MB says Jalur Gemilang flown without crescent moon and star was ‘unintentional’, ‘isolated’ incident
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the display of a Jalur Gemilang without its crescent and star at Dataran Batu Buruk was an isolated incident and was not deliberate. Berita Harian reported that he said the state government would investigate the matter after a video of the flag circulated on social media on Friday. He said MBKT would stop using stitched flags of that type and would instead buy fully finished flags to reduce the risk of a similar incident.
